ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC: Alain Resnais and Marguerite Duras Marguerite Duras (1914-1996) has, in the words of a New York Times essay about her, ?awed and maddened the French public for more than 40 years.? A colorful life, a rich filmography, a fantastic literary scribe, Duras?s works have the power to engage and, indeed, enrage. Her themes stretch from colonialism, to loss, to the bombing of Hiroshima, to love, and beyond. Alain Resnais (1922-2014), who collaborated with Duras on the creation of the cinematic masterpiece, Hiroshima, Mon Amour (1959), has made some of the classics of French cinema including Last Year At Marienbad (1961), and one of the earliest films about the Holocaust, Night and Fog (1955). This film and literature course will use these figures as springboards from which to examine larger questions of memory, trauma, loss, and the relationship between the past and present.
